tags.gist: Commends the paper as forward-thinking and agrees static validation paradigms cannot handle stochastic, emergent generative systems.
Argues from the writer's doctrine that governance must move from paper compliance to runtime enforcement, continuous benchmarking and immutable data lineage.
Says the paper moves in the right direction but omits runtime threat defense, data integrity and third-party model risk.
Endorses the two-axis matrix and its recognition that informational outputs may turn action-directing through wording, context and vulnerability.
Calls competency-based assessment modeled on credentialing sound and necessary, paralleling ongoing laboratory-style proficiency testing.
Agrees CDRH rightly emphasizes continuous postmarket surveillance and PCCPs, since premarket tests cannot predict every conversational path.
Calls accepting premarket uncertainty hazardous unless reduced evidence is strictly contingent on automated runtime boundary controls and kill-switches.
Says the paper underestimates indirect prompt injection through records and documents; wants pre-ingestion sanitization as a primary design control.
Citing a Part 11 audit-trail gap, would mandate a six-field chain-of-custody record per output, including model hash, prompts, retrieval lineage and clinician signature.
Proposes a three-tier materiality matrix where high-materiality anomalies trigger automated kill-switch, lockout, CAPA investigation and 24-hour reporting.
Calls master files insufficient and would require sponsors to secure 14-day advance notice and a sandbox to run golden tests before vendor updates go live.
Would add output reversibility and traceability as matrix dimensions, weighting irreversible surgical or pharmacological triggers more heavily.
Given saturation and leakage, wants sequestered sponsor-curated ground-truth sets judged by independent panels, with noisy, contradictory inputs.
Accepts evaluator agents for high-throughput monitoring if competency-qualified, rule-bound and subordinate to accountable human oversight.
Wants mandatory non-bypassable human checkpoints before irreversible agentic actions and isolated vector partitioning against cross-tenant data bleed.
Calls the paper a thoughtful foundation but says safety cannot rest on trust or after-the-fact monitoring; urges filtering, kill-switches and chain of custody.
